title: SEC Nigeria circular: Implementation of the IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards in Nigeria
citation: SEC Nigeria circular to all Public Companies and Significant Public Interest Capital Market Operators, published 23 September 2026, issued under the Investments and Securities Act 2025
evidence: Circular page, header line: "Published: September 23, 2026". The circular has no commencement clause, so the issue date is used. Opened https://home.sec.gov.ng/for-investors/keep-track-of-circulars/implementation-of-the-ifrs-sustainability-disclosure-standards-in-nigeria/ on 2026-11-02 (HTTP 200).
notes: Link only: NG-SEC-ADOPTED is permission requested (SEC website terms bar copying and reproduction; whether Copyright Act 2022 s. 3(b) covers a circular is open, see the row). Deviation from the brief: the circular is dated 2026-09-23, not 2024, and cites the Investments and Securities Act 2025 (the SEC front page says the President assented to the Investments and Securities Bill 2025, which repeals Act No. 29 of 2007). It directs every Public Company and Significant Public Interest Capital Market Operator to file an Implementation Plan by 15 October 2026 and restates the FRCN roadmap: voluntary adoption for periods beginning 1 January 2024 to periods ending 31 December 2027; mandatory for Public Interest Entities from periods beginning on or after 1 January 2028; SMEs from 1 January 2030. The FRC Nigeria roadmap is the plan behind those dates and is not a separate scope entry: https://frcnigeria.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/Roadmap-Report-for-the-Adoption-of-IFRS-Sustainability-Disclosure-Standards-in-Nigeria-Amended-2026-.pdf (found by search, not opened; the 2024 version is https://frcnigeria.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2024/07/FINAL-COPY-OF-SUSTAINABILITY-ROADMAP1.pdf). Nigeria's FRC site shows no terms page (the /terms-of-use and /privacy-policy guesses answered 404). English is the language of the circular; no translation looked for.

title: Climate Change Act 2021
citation: Climate Change Act, 2021 (Nigeria); establishes the National Council on Climate Change
evidence: No official page opened states the date. The National Council on Climate Change page says "Established by the Climate Change Act, 2021" (https://climatecouncil.gov.ng/, opened 2026-11-02, HTTP 200 with a browser user agent) and gives no assent or commencement date. The brief gives assent 2021-11-17; search results disagree (17 or 18 November 2021) and none is an official page.
notes: Link only: no official site opened serves the text. Looked for: nass.gov.ng Acts & Publications list (171 entries, no Climate Change Act; the bills tracker holds only Climate Change Bills of 2017 and 2019), justice.gov.ng (no laws section; site search found nothing), climatecouncil.gov.ng (home and documents pages, no Act file), copyright.gov.ng (no). Search results point to a gazette PDF in the ngfrepository.org.ng repository (a different publisher; the host reset the connection from the cloud address) and to private copies (PwC, KPMG, law firms, LawNigeria, judy.legal, UNEP LEAP, FAOLEX), none of which is stored. Row NG-NCCC-ADOPTED is permission requested. No government English translation is needed: English is the language of federal legislation.

title: National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency (Establishment) Act, 2007
citation: Act No. 25 of 2007, Federal Republic of Nigeria Official Gazette No. 92, Vol. 94, Lagos, 31 July 2007, A635-655 (re-cited Cap. N164 LFN 2010 in secondary sources)
evidence: The Act as printed in the gazette supplement carries the line "(30th Day of July,2007)" under the margin note "Commencement". Opened https://nesrea.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2025/05/NESREA-ACT.pdf on 2026-11-02 (HTTP 200, 314946 bytes, application/pdf). The NESREA FAQ says the Act was published in Gazette No. 92, Vol. 94 of 31 July 2007.
notes: Record text is the whole gazette supplement (22 pages) as extracted by pdftotext -layout with runs of spaces collapsed; the margin notes sit inside the lines of the section they annotate, and the gazette's own quotation marks come out as ― and ‖. The text is the Act as passed. Amended by the National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency (Establishment) (Amendment) Act 2018 (ng-nesrea-act-amendment-2018), whose PDF is an image scan, so no consolidated text is stored. The 2007 Act is the enabling statute for the NESREA regulations (including the air-quality, effluent and waste regulations listed on the same page), which are not in scope here. Language: en only; No government English translation is needed: English is the language of federal legislation.

title: Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Act 2018 (ss. 123 to 125: marketing standards and false or misleading representations)

evidence: Gazette supplement, margin note "Commencement": "[30th Day of January, 2019]" (OCR layer of the PDF at https://fccpc.gov.ng/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/FCCPA-2018.pdf, HTTP 200, 7842477 bytes, application/pdf, opened 2026-11-02).
